content.text:
I saved the recommendations to `recommendations.json`.

| Stage | Level | Main reason |
|---|---|---|
| prototype | **4** | The code gets thrown away and speed of learning matters most. Keep real credentials and real data out of it. |
| proof-of-concept | **3** | The demo has to work reliably and represent the product honestly, so test the paths you'll show and look for faked behavior. |
| mvp | **3** | Selective review overall, but read every line of auth, payments, data storage and user-input code. MVP code usually becomes production code. |
| production | **2** | The team has to own and maintain this code, so someone must understand every change, whether a person or AI wrote it. |
| critical | **2** | Every line gets reviewed, plus any extra checks your domain requires. Consider 1 or 0 for the most critical parts, and check whether your regulations say anything about AI-written code. |

**Two rules for every stage:**
- **Security-sensitive code always gets a line-by-line read** once real users or real data are involved.
- **Code must be re-reviewed before it moves to a later stage.** The most common real-world failure is a vibe-coded prototype that quietly becomes production.

I didn't put 0 or 1 as the default for any stage. Even in critical systems, the review requirement is what protects you, not who typed the code. Still, your team might reasonably choose 1 for certain components.
